newsitem.title: USA: GE Capital not in merger talks with Marsh.
newsitem.headline: GE Capital not in merger talks with Marsh.

text.p: GE Capital said on Tuesday it was not holding merger or acquisition talks with Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc.
GE Capital's comment came in response to a report in a British newspaper on Sunday that said Marsh insiders predicted a merger between the big U.S. insurance broker and General Electric.
"Though it is not our practice to comment on rumors, there are no merger or acquisition discussions with Marsh & McLennan," a GE Capital spokesman said. GE Capital is a unit of General Electric Co.
Marsh & McLennan declined comment, citing company policy.
The report in The Mail on Sunday, citing London sources, said Marsh wanted to link with General Electric to retain its position as the industry's biggest buyer of corporate and individual insurance.
But a GE Capital spokesman flatly denied the newspaper report.
GE Capital Services, a global financial services company based in Stamford, Conn., has acquired several large life insurers in the last few years and owns Employers Reinsurance Corp.
Marsh & McLennan, the world's largest insurance broker, agreed in March to acquire rival Johnson & Higgins.
Marsh & McLennan's agreement to buy Johnson & Higgins followed close on the heels of Aon Corp's December announcement that it had agreed to buy Alexander & Alexander.
Those deals have triggered speculation about further consolidation in the global insurance brokerage industry.
